blocks.text: Why Surface Wiping Alone Fails Without 4+ ACH HEPA Air Filtration

From October through March, seasonal Influenza A and B, RSV, human rhinovirus, and norovirus drive employee absenteeism across US commercial offices. Prior to modern indoor air quality updates from ASHRAE (Standard 241 Control of Infectious Aerosols) and the CDC, most office managers responded to cold and flu season simply by asking their night janitorial crew to wipe down door handles, elevator buttons, and faucet levers with a disinfectant rag at 8:00 PM. While nightly fomite disinfection is essential for enteric pathogens like norovirus and lingering staph or rhinovirus on shared keyboards and breakroom appliances, it cannot intercept airborne droplet nuclei (0.3 to 5 microns) exhaled during an eight-hour workday in an enclosed conference room.

Conversely, purchasing an under-sized consumer bedroom air purifier for a 2,500-square-foot bullpen—or skipping EPA-registered surface disinfection on breakroom microwave handles, conference phones, and restroom stall latches—leaves half the transmission pathway wide open. A commercial cold and flu season defense requires a synchronized dual-barrier kit: (1) high-CADR True HEPA H13 portable air scrubbers that cycle room air 2 to 5 times every hour during business hours, and (2) commercial-case EPA-registered disinfectant chemistry paired with zero-battery restroom odor control and antimicrobial entrance matting.

blocks.title: EPA Registration & Contact Dwell-Time Compliance in Commercial Offices
blocks.text: Under FIFRA and EPA List N guidelines, a disinfectant spray only achieves its 99.9% viral and bacterial kill claim if the treated surface remains visibly wet for the full label contact time (typically 30 seconds to 3 minutes for viruses, and up to 10 minutes for certain bacteria/fungi depending on the organism). Instruct staff and night custodians never to spray and immediately wipe bone-dry within 2 seconds.

blocks.text: Why This 5-Product Amazon Bundle Outperforms Ad-Hoc Janitorial Upcharges

When winter flu outbreaks hit an office, many janitorial contractors pitch 'electrostatic fogging' add-ons billed at specialty technician rates of $55 to $95 per hour ($250 to $500 per fogging visit). However, electrostatic spraying at 9:00 PM provides zero residual air filtration at 11:00 AM the next morning when twelve employees gather inside a conference room. Investing once in commercial H13 HEPA hardware and case-packed EPA disinfectants solves both the airborne and surface vectors every hour the office is occupied.

With a 950 CADR output and dual H13 True HEPA filters rated to capture 99.9% of airborne particles down to 0.1 microns (including influenza and coronavirus-laden respiratory droplet nuclei), a single Medify MA-112 Large Commercial Room HEPA H13 Purifier replaces three to four small residential units in an open office plan, eliminating power-cord clutter across cubicles. In enclosed conference rooms where background fan roar would disrupt client Zoom calls, the galvanized-steel Blueair Pro L Commercial Air Purifier combines electrostatic and mechanical HEPASilent filtration to deliver high airflow at whisper-low decibel levels and low electrical wattage. Staging the 12-pack case of Lysol Professional Disinfectant Spray (19-oz aerosol cans) alongside the Rubbermaid Commercial TCell 2.0 Continuous Odor Control System and the M+A Matting WaterHog Fashion 4x6 entrance mat ensures that every point of entry, every shared touchpoint, and every restroom stays protected throughout the 21.65 weekday cleaning cycles of each winter month.
5-Step Winter Flu Season Facility Execution Checklist
Roll out this five-step operational checklist on October 15 each year to lock in indoor air quality and high-touch disinfection before seasonal respiratory illnesses peak:

items.name: Audit Room Volume and Set HEPA Units to Deliver >= 4 ACH in Meeting Spaces
items.text: Place the Blueair Pro L inside your busiest 390-to-800-square-foot conference room and the 950-CADR Medify MA-112 in the central 2,500-square-foot open workstation hub. Lock the controls on medium-high during occupied hours (7:30 AM to 6:00 PM) so employees do not accidentally switch them off.

items.name: Stage 6 Cans of Lysol Professional 19-oz Spray at Daytime Touchpoint Hubs
items.text: Split your 12-pack case of Lysol Professional Disinfectant Spray: place six cans in public daytime zones (reception desk, breakroom counter, two main conference rooms, copy room, and wellness room) and lock the remaining six cans in the janitor closet for night crew restocking.

items.name: Pre-Clean Soiled Breakroom Surfaces Before Applying Disinfectant Spray
items.text: Train both employees and evening janitors that organic soil (coffee spills, food grease) blocks disinfectant efficacy. Wipe visible grease off breakroom counters ($12-$25/visit scope) first, then mist with Lysol Professional from 6 to 8 inches away until wet and allow full label contact dwell time.

items.name: Install Fresh 60-to-90-Day TCell 2.0 Refills at the Start of Q4 and Q1
items.text: Snap a new fuel-cell cartridge into every restroom Rubbermaid Commercial TCell 2.0 dispenser on November 1 and January 15 to guarantee continuous passive odor control across the entire winter heating season with zero battery changes.

items.name: Upgrade From 1x/Week or 2x/Week to 3x/Week or 5x/Week Cleaning During Peak Flu Months
items.text: If your office normally runs on a 1x-week (4.33 visits/month, 1.08x multiplier) or 2x-week (8.66 visits/month, 1.00x multiplier) schedule, step up to 3x-week (13.0 visits/month, 0.95x multiplier) or 5x-week (21.65 visits/month, 0.90x multiplier) from December through February so restrooms and breakrooms receive frequent professional disinfection.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a sanitizing claim and a disinfectant kill claim on Lysol Professional Disinfectant Spray?
faqs.a: Under EPA antimicrobial standards, 'sanitizing' a hard non-porous surface requires reducing specific bacterial populations by 99.9% within a shorter contact window (often 30 seconds), whereas 'disinfection' requires destroying 99.999% of listed bacteria, viruses (including Influenza A/B, Rhinovirus, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 on EPA List N), and fungi over the full required wet dwell time specified on the master label. Always require your night janitorial crew to follow the full disinfection wet-contact time on restroom fixtures ($15-$30/visit) and breakroom handles ($12-$25/visit).

faqs.q: Can we use Lysol Professional Disinfectant Spray on soft office surfaces like fabric conference room chairs and the M+A Matting WaterHog Fashion 4x6 mat?
faqs.a: Yes, for spot odor control and fabric bacterial sanitization where permitted by the product label. Unlike liquid bleach cleansers that strip dye from upholstery, Lysol Professional Disinfectant Spray can be lightly misted onto fabric reception seating and solution-dyed PET fibers like the WaterHog Fashion 4x6 mat to control odor-causing bacteria, while hard non-porous surfaces (door handles, phones, laminate tables, restroom porcelain) receive full EPA hard-surface disinfection.

faqs.q: Does OSHA require our janitorial vendor to provide PPE and SDS documentation when using aerosol disinfectants in our suite?
faqs.a: Yes. Under OSHA Hazard Communication Standard 29 CFR 1910.1200, the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for Lysol Professional Disinfectant Spray must be kept in the on-site janitorial SDS binder (or accessible via QR code), and custodians must wear appropriate nitrile gloves and eye protection when performing high-volume restroom disinfection. Furthermore, if a custodian cleans up any visible blood or body-fluid incident (such as vomit during a winter norovirus incident), OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard 29 CFR 1910.1030 rules apply.

faqs.q: How does frequency multiplier math make upgrading from 2x/week to 5x/week cleaning during winter more affordable than most office managers expect?
faqs.a: Commercial janitorial pricing rewards higher visit frequency with a lower per-visit cost multiplier because soil does not build up heavily between visits. Using 4.33 weeks per month, a 2x-week schedule (8.66 visits/month) is billed at a 1.00x base rate multiplier, whereas a 3x-week schedule (13.0 visits/month) drops to a 0.95x per-visit multiplier and a 5x-week daily weekday schedule (21.65 visits/month) drops to a 0.90x per-visit multiplier. On a 5,000-square-foot suite, the per-visit cleaning rate drops by 10% when moving from 2x/week to 5x/week.

faqs.q: How often do the H13 HEPA filters inside the Medify MA-112 and Blueair Pro L need to be replaced in a commercial office?
faqs.a: In a commercial office operating 10 to 12 hours per business day (roughly 2,500 to 3,000 run hours per year), commercial True HEPA H13 and HEPASilent filter sets should be replaced every 6 to 9 months—ideally installing a fresh filter set in October right before flu season begins and a second set in April when spring tree and grass pollen peaks. Never attempt to wash or vacuum a disposable H13 HEPA pleated filter cartridge, as moisture or vacuum suction destroys the micro-fiberglass electrostatic media structure.
